subject: EdgeFin private deployment: control plane, air-gap feasibility & next test plan

Subject: EdgeFin private deployment: control plane, air-gap feasibility & next test plan

Hi Alice — thanks again for a great discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear plan: 

What we heard from EdgeFin:
- Primary goal: run sensitive model inference in a private VPC or on-premise air-gapped environment for transaction risk scoring.
- Constraints: control plane must not traverse customer network in the air-gapped scenario; KMS keys managed by EdgeFin; strict egress controls; SLA expectations for sub-200ms p50 on common payloads.
- Competitors you are evaluating: hyperscaler-managed endpoints (AWS SageMaker endpoints), another inference API vendor, and a self-managed open-source runtime.

Redwood quick differentiators (high level):
- Unified API surface across hosted/dedicated/private so your app code doesn’t change between environments.
- Option A: Private control plane with customer-managed peering (VPC) — control plane traffic is over private links, we can restrict egress and integrate with your KMS.
- Option B: On-prem air-gap: we ship an offline bundle and a customer-side control plane agent; no outbound connections required once image and policy are installed.
- Operational features: token-level cost breakdown, per-model tracing, and automatic safe fallbacks to smaller quantized variants under load.

Suggested next tests (what would be helpful for qualification):
1) Network validation: we provide a control-plane network diagram and a short checklist (attached). You validate firewall rules and provide a staging switch we can test against.
2) Air-gap feasibility: a 2-day proof where we deploy our offline bundle in a restricted lab VM, validate start/stop, and demonstrate model loading and KMS integration using your staging HSM (or software KMS).
3) Latency baseline: run our standard 1k request synthetic workload in your staging environment (we provide client harness).

Proposed timeline: Network validation this week → air-gap lab test next week → latency baseline concurrently with the lab test.

Next actions for EdgeFin: reply with the preferred test window and any additional stakeholders (Darren, Ops, Security). Once you confirm, I’ll send over the PoC checklist, a scoped statement of work for the lab test, and a short NDA if needed.

Attachments: edgefin-controlplane-network-diagram.png, poc-integration-test-plan.md, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-quick-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

— Priyom
Priyom Das

- For the air-gapped test, we need the control plane to be demonstrably offline after install; can your bundle be hashed/signed so our infra team can verify integrity without contacting Redwood?
- For KMS: we plan to use our HSM (Thales) in staging. Will Redwood support HSM-backed key wrapping via standard PKCS#11 or a proxy?
- Hyperscaler question: AWS managed endpoints are easier initially but we’re worried about vendor lock and cost at scale. Can you share a short matrix on cost parity vs hyperscalers for batch vs real-time? (you attached something — thanks).

Stakeholders: please include Darren Lowe (Platform), and I’ll loop in SecurOps if we proceed with the air-gap test. Preferred test window: Oct 20–22 (PST).

Also, we prefer to sign a brief mutual NDA before exchanging detailed environment diagrams.

— Alice

Alice — quick technical notes from our infra/SE side ahead of the PoC: 

1) Offline bundle integrity: we sign the bundle with our release key and provide an SHA256 checksum; we can also provide an S/MIME-signed manifest for added verification. No outbound call is required for verification.

2) HSM/KMS: We integrate via a KMS proxy that supports PKCS#11 for HSMs — in the air-gapped mode the proxy runs on your side and wraps keys locally. We’ll need a short test harness that demonstrates wrap/unwrap cycles; I’ve included a minimal script in the attached poc-integration-test-plan.md.

3) Control plane architecture: two modes — (A) private control plane (customer VPC peering) where control messages use a private ENI and go over your peered link; (B) autonomous on-prem where control plane functionality is provided locally by the agent (no egress). See the attached network diagram for ports and CIDR ranges.

4) Hyperscaler comparison context: the attached matrix calls out typical cost buckets and where hyperscalers tend to add overhead (managed storage, model packaging, per-endpoint idle costs). For your real-time 200ms p50 requirement we expect better unit economics on dedicated GPUs when you have high sustained throughput; hyperscalers can be competitive at very low sustained usage due to managed infra.

Proposed technical checklist for Oct 20–22: 
- Day 1: Install agent and verify bundle signature; validate KMS proxy handshake with your staging HSM.
- Day 2: Load model artifact (we’ll provide a sample) and run 200 synthetic requests to measure cold and warm latencies; capture KV/cache behavior.
- Day 3 (optional): Run 1k parallel requests for throughput stress and confirm graceful fallback behavior.

I’ll be available for a 30–45m runbook walkthrough on Oct 19 if that helps SecurOps/Platform.

— Marissa
